summaryTr: The government significantly increased next year's budget to 821 trillion won based on the semiconductor boom.

editorial.body: 입력 이재명 대통령이 어제 김용범 청와대 정책실장의 사표를 수리했다. 지난달 30일 경제부총리와 국토교통부 장관 등 6개 부처의 장관을 교체할 때는 김 실장을 제외했다가 뒤늦게 경질 카드를 꺼냈다. 지지율 최저치를 경신하는 상황에 부닥친 이 대통령이 경제 정책 쇄신의 메시지로 반등의 기회를 마련하기 위해서는 불가피한 선택이었던 것으로 보인다. 단일 종목 레버리지 ETF로 인한 주식시장과 투자자 혼란, 부동산·세제 개편에 따른 여론 악화 등 국정 동력 약화에 대한 책임을 묻지 않을 수 없는 상황이었다. 그러나 경제 라인의 핵심들을 교체한 것만으로는 민심이 이반된 현 상황을 해결할 수 없다. 국민이 직접 체감할 수 있는 변화가 뒤따르지 않으면 인적 쇄신은 위기모면용 꼼수로 평가절하될 것이다. 정부가 어제 국무회의에서 비거주 1주택자의 세 부담을 강화했던 세제개편안을 철회한 것은 다행스러운 일이다. 정부는 비거주 1주택자의 기본공제 금액을 기존 정부 안(9억원)에서 현행(12억원)으로 유지했다. 비거주자의 부담을 강화했던 내용을 다시 완화한 것이다. 종부세 세 부담 상한도 현행 150%로 유지하기로 했다. 이 대통령은 “국민과 국회의 지적, 대안들을 대승적으로 검토하고 합당한 제안이 있다면 망설임 없이 입법과 예산에 충실히 반영해 달라”고 당부했다. 국민의 목소리를 정책에 반영하는 것은 너무 당연한 일이다. 정부·여당은 설익은 정책이 국민을 혼란에 빠트리고 지지율 하락을 자초한 이번 정책 실패의 경험을 집권 2년차의 교훈으로 삼아야 한다. 이 대통령은 각 부처에 레드팀의 시각을 주문했다. 기존 정책 속에 잘못된 부분을 찾아내는 방향으로 업무를 점검할 필요가 있다는 것이다. 일선 부처뿐 아니라 청와대에서도 레드팀은 작동해야 한다. 모든 정책을 만기친람형으로 살피고 지시를 내리는 이 대통령 자신에게도 적용해 보길 바란다. 거대 여당도 과연 레드팀이 작동할 수 있는 민주적이고 합리적인 의사 결정 구조를 갖추고 있는지 진단해 봐야 한다. 이재명 정부의 성공을 위해 필요한 것은 권력자의 눈치만 살피며 ‘원팀, 원보이스’를 외치는 과잉 충성이 아니라 불합리한 정책에는 과감하게 제동을 걸고 대안을 제시할 수 있는 소신과 실력이다.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: Tax Reform Reversal, Policy Chief Ousted...Lessons from Half-Baked Policy
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung reshuffles policy chief and withdraws tax reform plan to revamp economic policy.
Personnel reshuffle holds responsibility for confusion from hastily implemented policies and declining approval ratings.
Government and ruling party deem establishing a policy verification system through red team operations essential.
editorial.bodyTr: President Lee Jae-myung accepted the resignation of Kim Yong-beom, the presidential chief of policy, yesterday. When cabinet ministers from six departments, including the deputy prime minister for economy and the minister of land, infrastructure, and transport, were reshuffled last month, Kim was initially spared, but the president ultimately made the personnel change. Facing record-low approval ratings, President Lee appears to have made an unavoidable decision to signal an overhaul of economic policy and create an opportunity for a rebound. The situation left no room to avoid accountability for weakened national governance stemming from stock market and investor confusion caused by single-stock leveraged ETFs, and deteriorating public sentiment over real estate and tax reform. However, merely replacing key figures in the economic sector cannot resolve the current situation in which public sentiment has turned away. If actual changes that citizens can directly feel do not follow, personnel reshuffles will be downgraded as a gimmick for crisis management. It is fortunate that the government withdrew its tax reform plan at yesterday's cabinet meeting that would have strengthened the tax burden on non-resident single-property owners. The government maintained the basic deduction amount for non-residents at the current level of 1.2 billion won, rather than the proposed 900 million won. The government has again eased measures that would have increased the burden on non-residents. The ceiling on comprehensive real estate tax burden was also maintained at the current 150 percent. President Lee urged the government to "review suggestions from the people and National Assembly from a broader perspective and faithfully reflect reasonable proposals in legislation and budgeting without hesitation." Reflecting the voice of the people in policymaking is a matter of obvious necessity. The government and ruling party should learn from this policy failure, in which poorly formulated policies confused the public and hastened the decline in approval ratings, as a lesson for the second year of their administration. President Lee has ordered each ministry to adopt a red team perspective. The idea is to check operations by identifying errors within existing policies. Red teams should operate not only in line ministries but also within the presidential office. It is hoped that this principle will also be applied to President Lee himself, who scrutinizes all policies and issues directives. The ruling party should also diagnose whether it has a democratic and rational decision-making structure capable of operating a red team. What is needed for the success of the Lee Jae-myung administration is not excessive loyalty that watches only those in power and shouts "one team, one voice," but rather the conviction and competence to boldly apply the brakes to unreasonable policies and present alternatives.

editorial.title: Lopsided recovery
editorial.body: Conflicting fiscal and monetary policies leave vulnerable households stranded Economic recoveries tend to look better from a distance. South Korea is enjoying a semiconductor boom and is heading for its fastest annual growth in five years, yet many households are living in a far less forgiving economy. On Thursday, the Bank of Korea raised its benchmark rate by another 25 basis points to 3 percent, and lifted its 2026 growth forecast to 3.3 percent. For indebted households, neither figure offers much consolation. The problem is the uneven way inflation and interest rates hit household budgets. Consumer prices rose 2.8 percent in July from a year earlier, and core inflation reached 2.6 percent, its highest since December 2023. Essential food prices have been even more punishing. In the second quarter, rice rose 13.2 percent, potatoes 11.1 percent and eggs 9 percent. Prices of low-cost meals such as gimbap also rose faster than the overall consumer price index. Such increases matter more to poorer households because necessities consume a larger share of their income. Spending on food rose 6.9 percent among households in the second-lowest income quintile, compared with 1.8 percent for the 20 percent in the highest incomes. Interest costs show an even wider divide. Monthly interest expenses for the bottom 20 percent of households jumped 36.1 percent year on year in the second quarter, nearly three times the 12.1 percent increase for all households. Debt statistics reveal how quickly this strain is becoming entrenched. Nearly 97,200 people entered formal debt adjustment programs during the first half of this year. Among borrowers who were making payments under such arrangements, applications for small emergency loans reached 14,894 in the second quarter, the highest quarterly figure since 2022. A borrower who restructures a debt and then takes out another loan to cover living expenses is hardly on the road to financial recovery. This makes the policy mix particularly awkward. The BOK is tightening because inflation could broaden as the recovery strengthens. At the same time, the government is pursuing measures to ease financial burdens, including a planned 6 trillion won ($4.3 billion) debt relief program for struggling small-business owners and expanded lending through financial institutions. Assistance for people in genuine distress is necessary. But broad credit support can blunt the effect of monetary tightening, giving the central bank less room to ease rates. The result is a peculiar policy loop. Fiscal measures bolster demand, whereas monetary policy raises the price of money. The first boosts inflation, the second contains it. But they do not simply cancel each other out, because the effects are uneven. The risk is that those who can least absorb higher interest costs end up bearing the costs of both approaches. External pressures could complicate the dilemma. At the annual Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium in Moran, Wyoming, on Friday, new Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said underlying US inflation had not improved enough and emphasized the Fed’s responsibility for price stability. If US rates rise and Korea keeps its rate at 3 percent, the current 0.75 percentage-point gap could widen, putting renewed pressure on the won and raising import costs. Korea cannot assume that export strength will rescue domestic demand. July retail sales fell 2.4 percent despite semiconductor exports reaching $41 billion. A booming export sector can coexist with a struggling consumer economy. The Lee Jae Myung administration must make fiscal policy more precise. Direct support for households most in need would cushion hardship without adding unnecessary demand. Food prices require attention to supply and distribution. Debt programs should help viable borrowers regain solvency and allow unviable businesses to close, rather than merely rolling their loans forward. The chip boom has given Korea’s macroeconomic numbers a glossy finish. Household finances tell a more prosaic story. When groceries and debt cost more, aggregate growth offers little protection to those closest to the margin. The recovery may look broad in the national accounts, yet its costs remain unevenly distributed among households. summaryTr: 한국의 반도체 붐은 인플레이션과 증가하는 부채로 타격을 입은 어려운 가정 경제를 감춘다.
저소득 가정은 식료품에 6.9% 더 지출하는 한편 최저 소득층의 이자 비용은 36% 급증했다.

14,894건으로 2022년 이후 가장 높은 분기별 수치를 기록했다. 채무를 재구조화한 후 생활비를 충당하기 위해 다른 대출을 받는 차용자는 금융 회복의 길 위에 있다고 보기 어렵다. 이것이 정책 조합을 특히 어색하게 만든다. 한국은행은 경기 회복이 심화되면서 인플레이션이 확대될 수 있다는 우려로 긴축을 진행 중이다. 동시에 정부는 고민하고 있는 소상공인을 위한 6조 원의 계획된 채무 구제 프로그램과 금융 기관을 통한 확대된 대출을 포함한 금융 부담 완화 조치를 추진하고 있다. 진정한 어려움에 처한 사람들을 위한 지원은 필요하다. 하지만 광범위한 신용 지원은 금리 인하의 여지를 중앙은행에 덜 주면서 통화 긴축의 효과를 약화시킬 수 있다. 결과는 이상한 정책 루프다. 재정 정책은 수요를 촉진하는 반면 통화 정책은 자금 비용을 올린다. 전자는 인플레이션을 촉진하고 후자는 이를 억제한다. 하지만 영향이 불균등하기 때문에 단순히 상쇄되지는 않는다. 위험은 높은 이자 비용을 가장 적게 흡수할 수 있는 사람들이 두 접근 방식 모두의 비용을 부담하게 된다는 것이다. 외부 압력이 이 딜레마를 복잡하게 할 수 있다. 금요일 와이오밍주 모란의 연간 잭슨홀 경제정책 심포지엄에서 새로운 연방준비제도 의장 케빈 워시는 미국의 기저 인플레이션이 충분히 개선되지 않았으며 물가 안정에 대한 연준의 책임을 강조했다. 미국 금리가 올라가고 한국이 금리를 3%로 유지하면, 현재 0.75 포인트 격차가 확대되어 원화에 새로운 압력을 가하고 수입 비용을 높일 수 있다. 한국은 수출 강세가 국내 수요를 구할 것이라고 가정할 수 없다. 한다. 채무 프로그램은 실행 가능한 차용자가 지급 능력을 회복하고 실행 불가능한 사업이 폐업하도록 돕고, 단순히 대출을 연장하지 않아야 한다. 반도체 호황은 한국의 거시경제 수치에 광택을 입혔다. 가계 금융은 더욱 평범한 이야기를 말해준다. 식료품과 채무 비용이 더 많이 들 때 집계 성장은 한계에 있는 사람들에게 거의 보호를 제공하지 못한다. 회복은 국가 editorials.title: Lopsided recovery
editorials.body: Conflicting fiscal and monetary policies leave vulnerable households stranded Economic recoveries tend to look better from a distance. South Korea is enjoying a semiconductor boom and is heading for its fastest annual growth in five years, yet many households are living in a far less forgiving economy. On Thursday, the Bank of Korea raised its benchmark rate by another 25 basis points to 3 percent, and lifted its 2026 growth forecast to 3.3 percent. For indebted households, neither figure offers much consolation. The problem is the uneven way inflation and interest rates hit household budgets. Consumer prices rose 2.8 percent in July from a year earlier, and core inflation reached 2.6 percent, its highest since December 2023. Essential food prices have been even more punishing. In the second quarter, rice rose 13.2 percent, potatoes 11.1 percent and eggs 9 percent. Prices of low-cost meals such as gimbap also rose faster than the overall consumer price index. Such increases matter more to poorer households because necessities consume a larger share of their income. Spending on food rose 6.9 percent among households in the second-lowest income quintile, compared with 1.8 percent for the 20 percent in the highest incomes. Interest costs show an even wider divide. Monthly interest expenses for the bottom 20 percent of households jumped 36.1 percent year on year in the second quarter, nearly three times the 12.1 percent increase for all households. Debt statistics reveal how quickly this strain is becoming entrenched. Nearly 97,200 people entered formal debt adjustment programs during the first half of this year. Among borrowers who were making payments under such arrangements, applications for small emergency loans reached 14,894 in the second quarter, the highest quarterly figure since 2022. A borrower who restructures a debt and then takes out another loan to cover living expenses is hardly on the road to financial recovery. This makes the policy mix particularly awkward. The BOK is tightening because inflation could broaden as the recovery strengthens. At the same time, the government is pursuing measures to ease financial burdens, including a planned 6 trillion won ($4.3 billion) debt relief program for struggling small-business owners and expanded lending through financial institutions. Assistance for people in genuine distress is necessary. But broad credit support can blunt the effect of monetary tightening, giving the central bank less room to ease rates. The result is a peculiar policy loop. Fiscal measures bolster demand, whereas monetary policy raises the price of money. The first boosts inflation, the second contains it. But they do not simply cancel each other out, because the effects are uneven. The risk is that those who can least absorb higher interest costs end up bearing the costs of both approaches. External pressures could complicate the dilemma. At the annual Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium in Moran, Wyoming, on Friday, new Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said underlying US inflation had not improved enough and emphasized the Fed’s responsibility for price stability. If US rates rise and Korea keeps its rate at 3 percent, the current 0.75 percentage-point gap could widen, putting renewed pressure on the won and raising import costs. Korea cannot assume that export strength will rescue domestic demand. July retail sales fell 2.4 percent despite semiconductor exports reaching $41 billion. A booming export sector can coexist with a struggling consumer economy. The Lee Jae Myung administration must make fiscal policy more precise. Direct support for households most in need would cushion hardship without adding unnecessary demand. Food prices require attention to supply and distribution. Debt programs should help viable borrowers regain solvency and allow unviable businesses to close, rather than merely rolling their loans forward. The chip boom has given Korea’s macroeconomic numbers a glossy finish. Household finances tell a more prosaic story. When groceries and debt cost more, aggregate growth offers little protection to those closest to the margin. The recovery may look broad in the national accounts, yet its costs remain unevenly distributed among households. editorials.titleTr: Basic Pension Reform Promised, but Government Just Raised Spending While Keeping '70% Rule
summaryTr: The government promised basic pension reform but only increased spending in practice.
It raised payment amounts while keeping the eligibility criteria of the 'bottom 70% income bracket' unchanged.
It added 30,000 won for the bottom 30% and newly included 110,000 occupational pension recipients.
editorials.bodyTr: The government promised to reform the basic pension, but reform has gone nowhere and instead amounted to simply loosening the purse strings. The income-based eligibility criterion of the "bottom 70 percent," which was touted as the core of the reform, went untouched. Instead, the government merely increased the payment amounts. It will pay 380,000 won to the bottom 30 percent, 359,000 won to those in the 30th to 45th percentile, and maintain the current 350,000 won for the 45th to 70th percentile. The government newly included 110,000 occupational pension recipients and their spouses as eligible beneficiaries.
